claim: Platform transaction records for 2,299 paid livestream events by 1,165 Chinese creators show mean revenue of roughly USD 840 per event (mean price USD 2.97, mean 217.54 pre-period plus 64.77 post-period tickets) for a one-to-two-hour session.
stance_target: Establishing a measured, administrative-data per-event revenue figure for paid creator content, against which self-reported creator income can be checked
scope_conditions: Zhihu Live, China; events livestreamed November 2016-June 2017; platform-internal transaction data; excludes the ~10% of events the platform price-promoted; 30-day pre/post window capturing 85% of sales; platform revenue share not disclosed so this is gross ticket revenue, not creator take-home; NOT Southeast Asia
quoted_support: On average, an event is priced at around 3 USD (21 RMB), and has 218 tickets sold in the pre-livestream period and 65 in the post-period.

claim: Creator earnings in this administrative dataset are extremely right-skewed: the standard deviation of event sales is roughly twice the mean in both periods (424.72 vs 217.54 pre, 146.86 vs 64.77 post), confirming the mean-far-above-median income pattern in transaction records rather than self-report.
stance_target: The claim that creator income distributions are heavily right-skewed, so mean creator earnings systematically mislead about typical creator earnings
scope_conditions: Zhihu Live, China, Nov 2016-Jun 2017; 2,299 events; skew measured at event level, not creator level; the paper does not report a median or a Gini coefficient
quoted_support: Figure 2 further presents the distributions of prices and (log-transformed) aggregated pre- and post-period demand, showing substantial heterogeneity across events.

claim: Zhihu Live accumulated only about 10,000 events from 5,000 unique creators over four and a half years -- roughly two events per creator -- indicating that most vetted creators who enter paid livestreaming do not persist in it.
stance_target: The claim that most creators who begin monetized content production stop after very few attempts, a persistence problem visible even on a credentialed, gated platform
scope_conditions: Zhihu Live, China, May 2016 to December 2020 cumulative; figure cited by the authors from a secondary source (Fergus, 2020), not from their own data; the paper does not analyse creator survival and reports no churn rate, so this is an inference from aggregate ratios
quoted_support: By December 2020, Zhihu Live had nearly 10,000 Live events, 5,000 unique creators, and 6 million paying users

claim: Less-established creators with weaker reputational signals face a quantified pricing penalty: they gain disproportionately from post-event quality revelation, because consumer uncertainty suppresses their pre-event demand more than it does for reputed creators.
stance_target: The claim that reputation, not content quality alone, gates early creator earnings -- explaining why time-to-first-meaningful-income is long and why many quit before reputation accrues
scope_conditions: Zhihu Live, China, 2016-2017; instrumental-variables estimation with policy simulation under assumptions of creator sophistication and intertemporal demand independence; simulated rather than observed counterfactual
quoted_support: This gain is disproportionately larger for less-established creators with weaker reputational signals, for whom post-period quality revelation substantially alleviates consumer uncertainty.

claim: Post-livestream recorded sales account for 23% of total sales revenue, a monetization channel that creators and platforms systematically neglect by concentrating promotion on the pre-livestream window.
stance_target: The claim that measured creator revenue is understated by studies and creator self-reports that ignore back-catalogue and residual monetization
scope_conditions: Zhihu Live, China, Nov 2016-Jun 2017; 30-day post window; pay-per-view model, may not generalise to ad-supported or subscription platforms
quoted_support: although post-period demand is smaller, it still accounts for 23% of total sales, suggesting that post-livestream sales constitute an important revenue source for the platform and creators
numbers: 85% of total sales captured in the pre+post windows

claim: Zhihu Live gates entry on verified real name, educational background and proof of expertise, so its creator population is credentialed and not comparable to open-entry platforms like YouTube or TikTok where attrition is measured.
stance_target: The generalisation of persistence and income findings from vetted paid-content platforms to open-entry social video platforms
scope_conditions: Zhihu Live, China; entry requirements as documented by the authors for the 2016-2017 period
quoted_support: To become a Live creator, users need to provide Zhihu with basic personal information, such as real name, educational background, and proof of expertise in specific area(s).
numbers: seat limit 500 for over 95% of events
